# Record deployment-policy A2A observation in ADR 0038

## Context
The operator's own PAT reduced the visible Activity stream to that identity's mailbox. D19440 converged on an explicit, read-only team A2A view for the supported private single-operator deployment. This leaf records the decision before any dependent runtime policy lands; the outcome remains neomjs/neo-agent-institution#414.

## The Problem
[ADR 0038 §2.2 fact 4](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/38e9f095bfa994ba6d262b1cbf4d6ba83ba2c68c/learn/agentos/decisions/0038-fm-client-topology.md#L54) currently describes only independent content-grant edges. The already-shipped [sharing-policy resolver](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/197e659a667b57dabc6053786f1e8b11f054a2e6/ai/services/memory-core/helpers/resolveSharingPolicy.mjs#L30) also governs memories and summaries. The amendment must record that existing carrier and distinguish the new A2A list/detail right, rather than implying memory sharing already authorizes mailbox reads.

## The Architectural Reality
Design authority: D19440's accepted clause, “Select explicit team-content reads on the supported operator-controlled, private single-operator deployment, available to every admitted human or agent principal.”

The four identity facts stay separate. Deployment content policy is independent of per-target content grants; §2.3's grant-set coherence rule continues to govern those edges. The policy population is not claimed roster-coherent. Authentication and roster access never synthesize content rights. ADR 0038 is maintained in this repository; Brain owns runtime enforcement.

## The Fix
Amend `learn/agentos/decisions/0038-fm-client-topology.md` at §2.2 fact 4, §2.3 and relevant credential-use wording. Record existing memory/summary policy and newly authorized explicit A2A list/detail observation once, with a coherent amendment note and rejected alternatives. Keep the architecture guide's directly conflicting statements aligned where present; no new policy authority or runtime module.

The supported host trusts all callers admitted there. An unrelated valid PAT reaching the local surface is an admitted residual; loopback proves neither owned-agent membership nor same-user isolation. Shared, mixed-trust and exposed deployments need their own admission contract or private content policy. Do not invent a caller-controlled private-host flag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The amendment identifies the two independent content carriers, existing memory/summary behavior and new A2A authority without presenting future code as shipped.
- [ ] §2.3 is explicitly scoped to grant edges, with their coherence and lifecycle preserved; policy population is not declared roster-coherent.
- [ ] Grantees, explicit opt-in, private/legacy clamp, unchanged inbox defaults, no approval workflow and no peer mutation are stated together with the supported-host assumption and unrelated-local-PAT residual.
- [ ] Viewer/plane/effective-policy invalidation, retained archive history and retraction placeholders are recorded without inventing membership, host proof or a hard-delete filter.
- [ ] Relevant credential-use and architecture statements agree; the amendment names that it must merge before dependent runtime policy. The source comparison and both family signals are cited.

## Decision Record impact
Amends ADR 0038. Decision Record: REQUIRED — this leaf is the decision carrier, not runtime delivery.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping
Authority, profile boundary and content/roster separation → AC1–3. Canonical history and read-only behavior → AC4. Decision-before-runtime ordering → AC5. Runtime and installed acceptance remain the linked #414 delivery chain and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#490.

## Out of Scope
Runtime authorization changes, deployment configuration, grant administration, membership admission, a mail client, and mixed-operator support.

## Avoided Traps
Extending only credential text leaves fact 4 wrong. Treating team memories as current mailbox permission skips the new decision. Treating loopback or FM definitions as owned-agent proof reopens a withdrawn design.
